items.q: How do you install mattpocock/skills, and how big is the repo?
items.a: Run `npx skills@latest add mattpocock/skills` (Vercel skills.sh; Node required). At recording: **162K GitHub stars**, **7.5M downloads**, **38 skills** — works with Cursor, Codex, Claude Code. Prefer **project-scope** for teams, **symlink** copy mode.

Three things: **issue tracker** (local markdown, GitHub, Jira, Linear, Beads — just tell the agent which), **triage labels**, and **domain docs** (context.md + ADRs). Links land in CLAUDE.md pointing at `docs/agents/`.

sections.title: Main flow: grill → spec → tickets → implement

items.q: What sequence should you run for every piece of work?
items.a: Start with **grill-with-docs** (adversarial interview; demo asked 6 questions, typically ~**20**). If it fits one window → `/implement`. If multi-session → **`to-spec`** (destination) → **`to-tickets`** (journey) → implement per ticket with `/clear` between.

items.q: What's the difference between the spec and the tickets?
items.a: The **spec is the destination** (end state); **tickets are the journey** (how you get there). Each ticket is sized to **one context window / one smart zone** — e.g. one detailed spec with **11** sub-tickets, each a single session.

items.q: How expensive are 38 installed skills in the context window?
items.a: Because most are **user-invoked**, all 38 cost only **660 tokens** of description leak — short precise descriptions, most don't show up in `/context`.

items.q: Where does Opus 4.8 medium get "significantly dumber"?
items.a: Matt budgets the **smart zone** ending around **~140K tokens** — above that, attention degradation and weird hallucinations. Plan token budget per session (e.g. "we've got 100K of budget here").

items.q: How does the implement skill review code without rubber-stamping?
items.a: After type check + build, it loads **code review in sub-agents** on two axes: (1) work vs original **spec**, (2) repo **coding standards** (falls back to Fowler-style smells). Fresh context matters — agents are bad at improving code they just wrote.

items.q: What if you're new and don't know where to start?
items.a: Use **ask-matt** — "me as a skill," an onboarding oracle that knows the repo and prescribes the main flow with follow-ups. Grilling can start **vague**; answer until you've walked the whole tree, in auto mode not plan mode.
